title: Nondisclosure Agreement — Adams County Regional Water District and an unnamed "Company", executed 2024-01-10

provenance.evidence: Native text layer (PrimoPDF export of the executed copy, /Title "NONDISCLOSURE AGREEMENT"). The form is captioned "Nondisclosure Agreement (1/14)" on p.1 and "(10/13)" on p.2 — two revision stamps of the drafter's own template on one instrument, recorded as read.

parties.agency: ADAMS COUNTY REGIONAL WATER DISTRICT ("Agency") — a regional water district organized under R.C. Ch. 6119, 9203 SR 136 / P.O. Box 427, West Union, OH 45693. Signed by Rickey W. Adamson, General Manager, 1/10/2024. [verified] — the AGENCY box of the executed page is complete.
parties.company: ⚠️ NOT NAMED ANYWHERE IN THE INSTRUMENT. [verified] as an ABSENCE, read off the document: the recital reads "A company (together with its Affiliates or agents of any of the foregoing, collectively the 'Company') has approached you in connection with a project that may be located in _______" — the location blank is unfilled — and the notice block reads "Notices to Company will be delivered: Attn: [____________________]."
parties.company_identification_mechanism: §Preamble and the closing notice paragraph together make the anonymity a designed feature, not an oversight: "When the Company has revealed its identity to the Agency, all references to the 'Company' in this nondisclosure agreement will be deemed to be (a) references to the Company's actual legal entity ... and (b) CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION", and "The Company may change the foregoing notice information at any time and expects to provide new contact information ONCE IT HAS REVEALED ITS IDENTITY TO THE AGENCY."

board_action.body: Board of Trustees, Adams County Regional Water District
board_action.motion_verbatim: "to approve permission for Rick Adamson to sign a non-disclosure agreement for a company interested in purchasing and developing the former Stuart Generating Plant land"

authorization.sequence_note: ⚠️ THE SIGNATURE PRECEDES THE AUTHORIZATION BY ONE DAY. The executed page is dated 1/10/2024; the Board voted 2024-01-11. [verified] from two independent primary sources (the instrument's own agency box and the District's own minutes). This corpus records the discrepancy and does NOT resolve it — a one-day gap is equally consistent with a clerical date, a ratification practice, or a signature ahead of authority, and nothing in the corpus distinguishes them. ⚠️ Do not characterize it as unauthorized signing.

terms.statement_verbatim: "'Confidential Information' means all nonpublic information ... relating to Company or disclosed by Company or its Affiliates to Agency ... including THE NATURE, CONTENT, AND EXISTENCE OF THE PARTIES' COMMERCIAL RELATIONSHIP or discussions about a possible relationship or transaction, or any discussions or negotiations between the parties."
terms.note: The existence of the relationship is itself the secret. This is the clause that makes the District's own minutes read "the company" for two years.

terms.statement_verbatim: "Agency may disclose Confidential Information as required to comply with (a) orders of governmental entities with jurisdiction over it and (b) applicable freedom of information or public records laws, IF Agency (i) gives Company PRIOR WRITTEN NOTICE sufficient to allow Company to seek a protective order or other remedy ..., (ii) discloses only such information as is required by the governmental entity, and (iii) uses commercially reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment for any Confidential Information so disclosed."
terms.note: A private notice-and-object window bolted onto R.C. 149.43. ⚠️ It fixes NO number of days, unlike the five business days in Sidney's CRA §32 (data/extracted/sidney/). Whether such a clause is enforceable against Ohio's public-records act is a legal question this corpus does not answer; what is [verified] is that a public body agreed to it.

terms.statement_verbatim: "This Agreement is effective as of the date Confidential Information is first received and will continue for 3 years, after which it AUTOMATICALLY RENEWS unless either party terminates ... by providing at least 90 days prior written notice ..., provided, that Agency's obligations with respect to Confidential Information will survive for 5 years following termination ..., and Sections 6, 9, 10, and 11 will survive INDEFINITELY and the confidentiality obligations ... will continue to apply ... for as long as the information continues to constitute a trade secret."
"This Agreement will be governed by internal laws of THE STATE IN WHICH THE PROPERTY WHERE THE PROJECT IS TO BE BUILT IS LOCATED, without reference to its choice of law rules."
terms.note: Drafted to be signed before the site is known — the same posture as the unfilled location blank in the recital. [inference] that this is a multi-state siting template; nothing in the instrument says so.

terms.statement_verbatim: The executed copy carries a completed AGENCY box only. No Company signature, printed name, title, date or notice address appears anywhere on either page.

open_questions.question: Who is the "Company"? The corpus cannot answer from this instrument. The 2024-01-11 minutes describe it only as "a company interested in purchasing and developing the former Stuart Generating Plant land". By 2024-10-10 the District's minutes call the project "Project Galaxy"; by 2025-10-09 they retire that name. Buck Canyon Properties, LLC appears on the District's own plan set (route parcel #30, auditor parcel 1830000070002) and on the USACE jurisdictional determination — but NO instrument in this corpus joins that LLC to this NDA.
Does a countersigned copy exist? R.C. 149.43 request to ACRWD for the fully executed agreement, any amendment, and any §5 notice the District has given or received.
Has §5 ever been invoked — i.e. has the District notified the Company of a pending public-records request? That correspondence would name the counterparty.

title: Consent Order (Adams County C.P. 89-CIV-228)
warnings: Article V milestone (c) prints "August 2, 1993" with a stray overstrike mark immediately right of the "2" — a typewriter correction or scan artifact. The digit "2" itself is unambiguous at 600 DPI and no second digit is legible, so the date is recorded as 1993-08-02; verify against the page image before citing the day in a filing.

Three values on the instrument are HANDWRITTEN, not typed: the day and month in the entry line ("Entered this 29th day of June, 1993", p. 7), the resolution number (p. 10) and the resolution date (p. 10). The entry date is corroborated by the clerk's MECHANICAL file stamp and is [verified]; the resolution number and date rest on the handwriting alone.

The Village Clerk's PRINTED name appears nowhere in the instrument — only a signature on p. 10. It is left null rather than transcribed from the hand. The Mayor's name is printed (p. 8) and is not affected.

fields.agency: Ohio Attorney General (Environmental Enforcement Section), for the State of Ohio
fields.respondent: The Village of West Union, Ohio
fields.facility: Village of West Union wastewater treatment plant and sanitary sewer system, Adams County, Ohio. The order does NOT print a plant address or name a receiving water.
fields.stipulated_penalties: Two schedules (Art. XI), both per day and PER VIOLATION, payable by certified check to "Treasurer, State of Ohio" within 10 days of the failure (Art. XI.C). For the CONSTRUCTION milestones, Art. V(a)-(f): $100/day up to 30 days, $200/day for 31-60, $300/day for 60-90, $400/day over 90. For the COMPLIANCE milestone, Art. V(g): $500/day up to 30 days, $750/day for 31-60, $1,000/day over 60 — a 2.5x-to-5x step up from the construction tiers.
fields.status: unresolved in corpus — the published bytes are a 1993 snapshot. The court expressly RETAINED jurisdiction to enforce (Art. XII) and the instrument contains no termination provision at all (unlike the 1996 Allen County CWA decree, which conditions termination on 12 consecutive compliant months). Nothing in the corpus shows whether the 1995 milestones were met or whether jurisdiction was ever released.
fields.summary: Entered and filed 1993-06-29 in the Adams County Court of Common Pleas (Judge Elmer Spencer) on the State's 1989 complaint, resolving alleged violations of the discharge limitations and monitoring requirements of NPDES permit 0PC00019*CD and of R.C. Chapter 6111. Three injunctions run together: immediate compliance with R.C. Ch. 6111 and the permit (Art. IV.A); Appendix "A" interim effluent limits until 1994-10-03 and the permit's final effluent standards after (Art. IV.B/C); and elimination of all sanitary-sewer overflows and bypasses plus completion of the WWTP improvements described in the Facilities Plan submitted to Ohio EPA on 1992-05-26, on a seven-milestone schedule ending 1995-05-01 (Art. V). $5,000 civil penalty, stipulated penalties on every milestone, and reporting to Ohio EPA's Southeast District Office within 7 days of each milestone date.

obligations.requirement: Initiation of Project Design Work (Art. V(a))
Submittal of Approvable Plans and Specifications to Ohio EPA (Art. V(b))
Completion of construction of sufficient wetstream treatment facilities to ensure compliance with final effluent limits, and to eliminate all bypasses and overflows from the system (Art. V(f))
Attain compliance with final effluent limitations (Art. V(g))
Comply with the Appendix "A" interim effluent limitations (Art. IV.B)
Meet the final effluent standards of NPDES 0PC00019*CD (Art. IV.C)
Written report to Ohio EPA Southeast District Office, Division of Water Pollution Control, 2195 Front Street, Logan, Ohio 43138, stating whether each milestone was performed (Art. VII)
obligations.deadline: 7 days from each milestone completion date

obligations.requirement: Pay the $5,000 civil penalty by certified check to "Treasurer, State of Ohio" (Art. X)
Properly operate and maintain the WWTP and any associated equipment and structures (Art. IV.D)
Provide a copy of the Consent Order to each contractor employed on the work, and require each general contractor to provide a copy to its subcontractors (Art. II)

fields.note: [verified] All figures, dates and codes read from the instrument's own page images. The order is entered "without trial of any issue of fact or law, and upon consent of the parties" (p. 1), so the State's characterization of the Village's conduct is an allegation the order RESOLVES, not a finding it makes — see `alleged_violations`. Compliance with the order's terms constitutes full satisfaction of civil liability for all claims alleged in the Complaint (Art. III.B), but does not limit the State as to claims not alleged, including violations occurring after the filing (Art. III.C).

vote.ballot_method: ballots/proxies, counted by inspectors appointed by the President

disclosures.statement_verbatim: "Richard Seaman, Jr., announced that the customers had approved, by a vote of 579 yes and 141 no, in favor of the amendment of the Articles of Incorporation to convert the corporation to a Chapter 6119 Regional Water Authority, to change the name of the corporation to Adams County Regional Water District, Inc."
disclosures.note: 80.4% in favor on 720 votes cast. What was traded is visible only by reading this document against the by-laws that followed: under the predecessor company the trustees were ELECTED by the members at this very meeting, by petition and ballot, with vote totals published. Under the 1994 by-laws the board "shall be composed as per the Entry of the Court", and vacancies are filled by a three-trustee nominating committee and a two-thirds vote OF THE TRUSTEES. ⚠️ Nothing in this corpus records what the members were told the conversion would mean for their franchise; the minutes report the result, not the campaign.

Attorney David Wilson swore in the Trustees and administered the oath of office."

fields.instrument: Ohio Level Two Isolated Wetland Permit
fields.issuing_office: Ohio EPA, Division of Surface Water, 401/Wetlands/Mitigation Section, Columbus

permittee.name: 68 Yards, LLC
permittee.note: ⚠️ THE FIRST DOCUMENT TO GIVE 68 YARDS, LLC A PRINCIPAL AND AN ADDRESS. The corpus carried the name only from the USACE NWP 39 verification, with its affiliation to Buck Canyon Properties, LLC / Derek Harmon `[open]`. That affiliation is STILL `[open]` — this permit does not connect the two entities either; it just shows they hold different instruments on the same project. A ProtonMail address on a permittee of a project of this scale is recorded as a fact, and no inference is drawn from it.

project_description.note: ⚠️ THE STATE'S OWN DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT, and it is NOT "data center". Adams County's government domain (amazon.adamscountyoh.gov) calls this an Amazon Web Services campus; Ohio EPA's granted permit calls it a light industrial park. Both are primary. The corpus records the discrepancy and does NOT resolve it — a generic land-use description on an environmental permit is ordinary practice and is not evidence of concealment, and it is equally not corroboration of the end use.

watershed.verbatim: "The project is partially located in two watersheds: The project is located in the Cabin Creek - Ohio River Watershed (HUC 05090201-06). Crooked Creek has a designated aquatic life use of warmwater habitat (WWH), agricultural water supply (AWS), industrial water supply (IWS), and primary contact recreation (PCR) water."
watershed.note: ⚠️ CORROBORATES THE ROUTE-BLIND FINDING. The state places this project in the Cabin Creek-Ohio River watershed, not on Ohio Brush Creek — while `SiteProfile.nwis_sites` screens Ohio Brush Creek gage 03237500. A dilution screen on that gage answers a question about a different watershed. Recorded verbatim including the permit's own "partially located in two watersheds", which it does not enumerate.

antidegradation.verbatim: "I have determined that a lowering of water quality in the Ohio Brush-Whiteoak watershed (HUC 05090201) as authorized by this permit is necessary."
antidegradation.note: The R.C. 6111 antidegradation determination — the state finding that the permitted water-quality loss is necessary. Note it names the HUC-8 (Ohio Brush-Whiteoak, 05090201) while the setting paragraph names the HUC-12 (05090201-06); they are nested, not conflicting.

impacts.note: ⚠️ THESE ARE **ISOLATED** WETLANDS AND ARE A SEPARATE ACCOUNT FROM THE FEDERAL FILL. The USACE NWP 39 verification authorizes 0.06 ac of two JURISDICTIONAL wetlands (E and G) plus 1,893 linear feet of four streams. This permit authorizes 0.74 ac of seven ISOLATED wetlands (B, D, F, H, I, J, K) that are outside federal jurisdiction post-Sackett. The wetland ids do not overlap, which is consistent with one delineation split between two authorities. ⚠️ NEVER SUM THE TWO into a single "wetland impact" figure without saying which authority each half sits under.

title: West Union Wastewater Treatment Plant
warnings: THE RECEIVING WATER IS NAMED TWO DIFFERENT WAYS ON THE FACE OF THE SAME PDF. The authorization sentence (sheet 1), the Fact Sheet header, and Attachment I's location paragraph all say "Beasley Creek" (3 occurrences, no "Fork"). The Part II Item B sampling-station table (sheet 10) names the SAME water "Beasley Fork Creek" three times, at stations 001, 801 and 901 (3 occurrences, with "Fork"). This file transcribes each exactly as printed where it appears rather than harmonizing the name; see receiving_water_note and sampling_stations below.

THE FACILITY ADDRESS IS PRINTED TWO WAYS. The sheet-1 authorization sentence gives "6875 State Route 247, West Union, Ohio, Adams County" (no directional suffix, no ZIP). The Fact Sheet (bound into this same PDF) gives "6875 State Route 247 South, West Union, OH 45693" — adding "South" and the ZIP code. Same facility, same road; the document does not explain the "South" suffix. Transcribed as printed at each location.

THIS PERMIT CONTAINS NO PART I.C SCHEDULE OF COMPLIANCE. Unlike the Mansfield precedent (which carries a Toxicity Reduction Evaluation and a Municipal Pretreatment Schedule), Part I of this permit ends at Part I.B (the non-outfall monitoring tables, sheets 4-8) and Part II, "Other Requirements," begins directly on sheet 9. There is no whole effluent toxicity (WET) limit anywhere in this permit, no biomonitoring program item, no pretreatment schedule, and no numeric bypass-volume trigger — this is a materially smaller and simpler instrument than the Mansfield one. See no_schedule_of_compliance below for the explicit absence.

THE PDF HOLDS 33 PAGES; THE PERMIT'S OWN "Total Pages" READS 27. This reconciles cleanly and is not a defect: sheets 1-27 (PDF indices 0-26) are the permit itself (Parts I-III), each headed "Page N / 0PC00019*KD" — 27 pages, matching the printed count exactly. PDF indices 27-32 (6 more pages) are the bound-in Fact Sheet plus Attachments I and II; none of those 6 pages carries the permit's "Page N" header or is counted in "Total Pages: 27". See fact_sheet_and_attachments below.

ATTACHMENT II'S FOOTNOTES SKIP "b". The table cites footnote "a" (design flow) and footnote "c" (the Basis-code legend on the following page) but no footnote "b" appears anywhere on either page — a gap in the document's own lettering, not a transcription omission. Checked in both default and layout-mode extraction of both pages. The same design-flow note also carries a DIFFERENT marker in each table for the same fact: Part I.A marks it "*" (bound to the column header "Loading* kg/day", sheet 2; see effluent_limits_001.footnotes) while Attachment II marks the identical note "a" — one document, two footnote-lettering conventions for the same note.

FREE CYANIDE'S UNITS DISAGREE BY 1000× BETWEEN THE TWO EFFLUENT-LIMIT TABLES. Part I.A (sheet 3) prints "51173 - Cyanide, Free (Low-Level) - ug/l"; Attachment II (PDF idx 31) prints the same monitor-only parameter as "Cyanide, Free ... mg/l" — a milligram value, where this permit's own Part II Item I sets the free-cyanide PQL at 0.025 mg/L (sheet 12). Neither table carries a numeric limit here (both monitor-only), so there is no live compliance conflict, but the unit disagreement is real and internal to this one committed document — re-checked in extraction_mode="layout" for both pages. See effluent_limits_001.limits.cyanide_free_low_level and effluent_limits_001.cross_check.

effluent_limits_001.cross_check: Attachment II, "Final Effluent Limits for Outfall 0PC00019-001" (bound into this same PDF, sheet unnumbered / PDF page 32), reprints every one of the 23 parameters above under a different column layout (30 Day Average / Weekly Average / Daily Maximum / Daily Minimum, plus a "Basis" code) and every NUMERIC figure and column placement agrees exactly with Part I.A — re-checked in extraction_mode="layout" for both tables. ONE thing does NOT agree: free cyanide's units (ug/l in Part I.A, mg/l in Attachment II — see warnings[5] and limits.cyanide_free_low_level). Basis codes as printed: pH, Dissolved Oxygen, Oil & Grease, E. coli and Peracetic Acid = WQS; Total Suspended Solids and CBOD = BADCT; Ammonia (Summer) and Copper = WLA; every OTHER monitor-only parameter = M (per "Division of Surface Water NPDES Permit Guidance 1: Monitoring frequency requirements for Sanitary Discharges") EXCEPT Ammonia (Winter), which is monitor-only but coded WLA, not M — Ohio EPA ran a wasteload allocation for winter ammonia and elected monitor-only, a materially different regulatory posture from the generic monitoring-frequency guidance that covers the rest. This is agreement within the one committed document, not a second source — see fact_sheet_and_attachments below.

sso_300.parameter: Overflow Occurrence (74062), No./Month, 1/Month Total, all months
sso_300.note: The permit is explicit that the 1/Month frequency is a REPORTING frequency, not a monitoring one: "these overflows shall be monitored on each day when they discharge." Only SSOs that reach waters of the state — directly or through a storm sewer — are reported at this station; each location overflowing on a given day counts as one occurrence.
sso_300.annual_report: An annual SSO report covering ALL overflows in the collection system is due March 31 for the prior calendar year, with locations numbered consecutively from 301, volumes in millions of gallons, and a narrative water-in-basement analysis.
sso_300.prohibition: Part II Item D itself (sheet 10) states a flat prohibition, distinct from the reporting/monitoring machinery around it: "All SSOs are prohibited." The station-300 table's own Notes (sheet 4, footnote c) independently state the same thing: "All sanitary sewer overflows are prohibited." One of this instrument's few absolute conditions, not merely a reporting requirement.
sso_300.submission_district_office: Part II Item D.2(b) names where the hardcopy alternative to electronic submission goes: "you may submit one hardcopy of the report to Ohio EPA Southeast District Office and one copy to: Ohio EPA; Division of Surface Water; NPDES Permit Unit..." This is the one place in this instrument that identifies a specific Ohio EPA district office for this facility (Adams County) — unlike the Mansfield precedent [reference], where the district office was left [open].

monitoring_stations.sludge_588_note: Station 0PC00019588 (sludge transferred to another NPDES permit holder in an emergency) is authorized in Part II Item O but, as the permit itself says, "the table is not included in Part I.B for this station" — it is reported only on the Annual Sludge Report, not on the DMR.

monitoring_stations.same_day_sampling_rule: Part II Item L (sheet 13): "Sampling for these parameters at station 0PC00019001, 0PC00019601, and 0PC00019901 shall occur the same day." As printed, this ties effluent, influent and downstream sampling together but does NOT name station 801 (upstream) — transcribed as printed rather than assumed to be an omission. This is an internal contradiction, not just a drafting gap: station 801's own Part I.B footnote (sheet 7) reads "Sampling Events - See Part II, Item L," pointing 801 at the very Item L rule that excludes it by name.

outfall_signage.requirement: A permanent stream-bank marker at every regulated outfall — minimum 2 ft x 2 ft, at least 3 ft above ground, letters at least 2 inches tall, naming the permittee, the Ohio EPA permit number, the outfall number and a contact phone number.

other_requirements_of_note.biomonitoring_and_pretreatment_note: This permit has no biomonitoring-program item and no pretreatment item (compare Mansfield's Items T and U) [reference] — the letter sequence in Part II runs A through S and stops there.

general_conditions_part_iii.note: A standard 32-item Ohio EPA general-conditions boilerplate (Definitions, General Effluent Limitation, Facility Operation and Quality Control, Reporting, Sampling and Analytical Method, Recording of Results, Records Retention, Availability of Reports, Duty to Provide Information, Right of Entry, Unauthorized Discharges, Noncompliance Notification, RESERVED, Duty to Mitigate, Authorized Discharges, Discharge Changes, Toxic Pollutants, Permit Modification or Revocation, Transfer of Ownership or Control, Oil and Hazardous Substance Liability, Solids Disposal, Construction Affecting Navigable Waters, Civil and Criminal Liability, State Laws and Regulations, Property Rights, Upset, Severability, Signatory Requirements, Other Information, Need to Halt or Reduce Activity, Applicable Federal Rules, Availability of Public Sewers) — all 32 named. Item 13, "RESERVED," is a placeholder carrying no substantive text of its own. Indexed here rather than walked item by item; two items carry facility-independent numeric content worth recording:

unauthorized_discharges.note: Bypass not exceeding limitations is allowed only for essential maintenance to assure efficient operation; bypass causing an exceedance is otherwise prohibited unless unavoidable to prevent loss of life/injury/severe property damage, with no feasible alternative, and with notice given. NO numeric flow threshold is attached to this provision anywhere in the permit — see other_requirements_of_note.bypass_provisions_note.

penalties.note: Cites ORC 6111.99: falsifying or tampering with required monitoring devices or methods, or knowingly making a false statement/certification in a required record or report, is punishable by a fine of not more than $25,000 per violation upon conviction; violating ORC 6111.04, 6111.042, 6111.05 or 6111.07(A) is punishable by a fine of not more than $25,000, imprisonment of not more than one year, or both.

general_conditions_part_iii.noncompliance_notification_districts_not: Item 12 lists all six Ohio EPA district-office emergency contacts (Southeast, Southwest, Northwest, Northeast, Central District, Central Office) as generic boilerplate — it does not itself identify which one covers this facility. The one place this permit DOES name a specific district office for this facility is Item D.2(b) (see monitoring_stations.sso_300.submission_district_office).
